newsitem.title: THAILAND: Fin One wants to sell shares to Thai central bank.
newsitem.headline: Fin One wants to sell shares to Thai central bank.

text.p: Thailand's ailing Finance One Plc said on Monday it wants to sell 827.62 million capital increase shares, which have not yet been subscribed to by existing shareholders, to the central bank.

Only 617,726 shares had been subscribed to by its shareholders during the subscription period of 828.24 million shares that had been offered, Finance One said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.
The Bank of Thailand originally said it would buy shares from Finance One but later said it would not and stressed it wanted the firm to be merged.

Debt-ridden Finance One, once the country's largest finance company, is one of 16 finance firms which the central bank suspended on Friday in order to force their merger with other healthy finance firms.
Brokers said investors had declined to buy Finance One's new shares because its offer price was much higher than the market price.
Finance One on Thursday closed at 3.80 baht, while its offer price was set at 7.50 baht.
The bourse has suspended trading in Finance One shares since Friday following the central bank's suspension of its operations.
